summary: Backend-only verification of the 'backend aiortc PC now uses Cloudflare TURN' fix. Wrote 6 in-process pytest unit tests for stream._new_pc_with_extra_ice() (introspecting aiortc's private _RTCPeerConnection__configuration) and a new E2E script that runs a hit-counting mock Cloudflare TURN endpoint (port 9739 + CF_TURN_ENDPOINT in backend/.env + supervisor restart, cleaned up afterwards), configures CF via PUT /api/stream/turn/cloudflare, then publishes via /api/whip and subscribes via /api/whep with aiortc. Results: mock hit once during /api/whip (backend PC), once for GET /api/stream/ice-servers, and once more during /api/whep => 3 mints, all within 10s of the WHIP POST. Provider-raises and provider-returns-empty paths both fall back to static STUN identically to _new_pc(). All 5 legacy suites (test_whip_whep, test_whip_auth, test_chat_and_lock, test_toy_relay, test_cloudflare_turn) exit 0, and 41/42 existing stream pytest tests passed (the one failure was a stale assertion in the test suite itself, fixed).

minor.issue: PERF/RESILIENCE only (not a failure observed in tests): with Cloudflare configured, every WHIP/WHEP request now makes a synchronous outbound POST to Cloudflare (httpx timeout=8s in cloudflare_turn.mint_ice_servers). In /api/whip this await happens while holding hub.lock, so a slow/unreachable Cloudflare API can stall publish/takeover for up to 8s and serialize concurrent viewers. Consider a short-TTL cache of minted creds (they are valid 1h) and/or a tighter timeout (~2-3s).

action_items: Optional: cache minted Cloudflare TURN creds (1h TTL) instead of minting on every WHIP/WHEP PC creation, and move the mint outside hub.lock in the WHIP handler.
critical_code_review_comments: stream.py: module-level `_get_extra_ice_servers` is declared at line 231, i.e. AFTER _new_pc_with_extra_ice() (line 95) references it. It works (global resolved at call time) but is fragile/confusing — move the declaration above the function.
cloudflare_turn.mint_ice_servers uses timeout=8; on the WHIP path this runs under hub.lock. A minted credential is valid 1h, so per-PC minting is wasteful — cache it.
stream.py is 530 lines — still under the 700-line threshold, no split needed yet.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_stream_ice_stun.py (fixed stale assertion: test_call_sites_use_new_pc counted only '_new_pc()' occurrences and failed after WHIP/WHEP switched to '_new_pc_with_extra_ice()'; now counts both variants and asserts the async variant is used)

success_rate.backend: 100% (6/6 new unit tests, 1/1 new E2E, 5/5 legacy scripts, 42/42 stream pytest after test-code fix)

rca_of_the_issue: Original bug: backend PCs were built by the sync _new_pc() which only read env STUN/TURN, so the server side never had the Cloudflare relay and ICE failed for carrier-NAT viewers. The fix (async _new_pc_with_extra_ice() + set_extra_ice_provider wired to cloudflare_turn.get_ice_servers_for_viewer) is confirmed working: the mock Cloudflare endpoint is hit once per backend PC creation (WHIP and WHEP) with the CF TURN entry appended to the static STUN list, and failures/empty results degrade to static ICE without raising.
